data.title: Nestmedic’s PregnaOne 510(k) Moves Into Substantive FDA Review
data.description:
Nestmedic SA ( (PL:NST) ) has provided an update.

Nestmedic has moved to a new phase in its U.S. regulatory push, as the Food and Drug Administration has formally accepted its 510(k) submission for the PregnaOne system and assigned a Lead Reviewer under number K263053. The file is now under substantive review in the Office of Health Technology 3B, the unit responsible for obstetrics and reproductive health devices, marking a key milestone but not yet implying marketing approval.

The company notes that FDA may request further data or clarifications during a possible Substantive Interaction and expects the next major contact with the regulator in about 45 days, in line with typical timelines. Management views this progress in the 510(k) process as an important step in executing its strategy to introduce PregnaOne to the U.S. market, a priority growth avenue for the firm, and will report subsequent significant regulatory developments as required.

data.title: Reabold’s Union Jack Bid Loses Board Backing as Acceptances Remain Low
data.description:
An update from Reabold Resources ( (GB:RBD) ) is now available.

Reabold Resources has clarified that its previously recommended all-share offer for Union Jack Oil is no longer backed by Union Jack’s new board, following the publication of a formal rejection circular on 11 September. The company nonetheless continues to pursue the takeover, arguing that Union Jack’s assets would benefit from integration into a stronger, more competitive and better-funded business.

As of 14 September, Reabold had secured valid acceptances for about 5.70 per cent of Union Jack’s issued share capital, including shares subject to irrevocable undertakings, leaving the offer a long way from control. The UK Takeover Panel has reset the final acceptance deadline to 2 October, giving Reabold a short window to increase support among Union Jack shareholders and determine whether the bid can reach the required acceptance condition.

data.title: SMJ International Holdings Shareholders Approve Governance Changes at September 15 EGM
data.description:
SMJ International Holdings Inc. Class A ( (SMJF) ) has issued an announcement.

SMJ International Holdings Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted company with its principal executive office in Singapore, operates under a dual-class share structure that allocates one vote per Class A Ordinary Share and ten votes per Class B Ordinary Share. This structure supports a concentrated voting framework for key holders and shapes the company’s governance dynamics as a foreign private issuer in U.S. markets.

On September 15, 2026, SMJ International Holdings Inc. held an extraordinary general meeting in Singapore, where shareholders approved a second amended and restated memorandum and articles of association. The changes remove certain automatic conversion triggers for Class B to Class A shares, lower the threshold for written ordinary resolutions, and streamline voting procedures, while authorising the board to complete all necessary implementation steps, signaling a move to refine control and modernize governance for stakeholders.

data.title: 2CRSi’s Independent Expert Confirms German Server Sale Amid Short-Seller Allegations
data.description:

2CRSi SA has released initial findings from an investigation by an independent expert into a major German order for 194 Godì Blackwell Ultra servers, following allegations raised by the fund Grizzly Research. The expert’s review of contractual and financial documentation confirms the existence of the order placed on 7 May 2026, the corresponding supplier purchase and that the full sale price and supplier payment were received and made before delivery.

The company states that the entire transaction was properly recorded in its accounts for the financial year ended 30 June 2026, addressing concerns over the reality of this €110 million German sale.
